slide-1.description: Drop kerbs allow people to transition from the footpath to the street. They should exist at all crossable intersections.

slide-2.description: Driveways are not drop kerbs. They are designed for vehicles and not pedestrians. Driveways should not be labeled as Drop Kerbs.

slide-3.description: Driveways to garages are not drop kerbs. Driveways should not be labeled as Drop Kerbs.

slide-1.description: Footpath intersections should have drop kerbs—ideally two per corner. If a corner has a footpath but does not have a drop kerb, place the Missing Drop Kerb label where you think a drop kerb should exist.

slide-2.description: Residential walkways should not be labeled as Missing Drop Kerbs.

slide-3.description: Drop Kerbs are not needed at paths not intended for pedestrians to pass.

slide-4.description: For corners with no footpaths, use the No Footpath label rather than a Missing Drop Kerb label.

slide-2.title: Ample space to manoeuvre around
slide-2.description: The motorcycle is parked on the side; there is ample space for pedestrians on the remaining space of the footpath.

slide-3.title: Obstacle not on footpath
slide-3.description:
This traffic cone is not on a pedestrian pathway so it should not be marked as an Obstacle.

Only mark obstacles on footpaths, pedestrian crossings, and other pedestrian pathways.

slide-1.description: If something on the footpath or pedestrian crossing surface would make it uncomfortable or impossible to cross, it should be labeled as a Surface Problem.

slide-2.title: Normal footpath tiles
slide-2.description: Normal footpath tiles (without gaps, cracks or bumps) are not surface problems.

slide-3.description:
This gravel is not on a pedestrian pathway so it should not be marked as a Surface Problem.

Only mark surface problems on footpaths, pedestrian crossings, and other pedestrian pathways.

slide-1.description: If a street side does not have a footpath, please mark it with a No Footpath label.

slide-2.description: A median that separates two directions of a traffic and is not intended for pedestrians should not be labeled as No Footpath.

slide-3.description: There is a footpath here. It should not be marked as No Footpath.

slide-1.description:
A pedestrian crossing is a legally defined space to cross a road.

Pedestrian Crossings are often indicated by parallel dashed lines.

slide-2.description: Crossings with no visual indicator should not be labeled as Marked Pedestrian Crossings.

slide-3.description: Stop lines for cars should not be labeled as Marked Pedestrian Crossings.

slide-4.description: Speed bumps should not be labeled as Marked Pedestrian Crossings.

wrong-type.tooltip-curb-ramp: Sometimes a missing drop kerb is accidentally mislabeled as a drop kerb
wrong-type.tooltip-no-curb-ramp: Sometimes a drop kerb is mislabeled as a missing ramp, often because it's missing a tactile warning
wrong-type.tooltip-surface-problem: Gravel or grass are not considered a footpath, and should be marked with a No Footpath label
wrong-type.tooltip-no-sidewalk: Surface problems or obstacles may be mistakenly labeled as No Footpath

driveway-transition.text: This is a footpath to driveway transition
driveway-transition.tooltip: Footpath to driveway transitions are not drop kerbs unless a dedicated ramp has been added

unsafe-crossing.tooltip: Pedestrians are not meant to cross at this spot, so no drop kerb is expected

not-pedestrian-path.tooltip-obstacle: If there is no footpath or the object is not on the part of the footpath meant for pedestrians, like in the image below, an Obstacle label is not needed

ample-space.tooltip: On very wide footpaths, easily avoidable objects should not be labeled as obstacles

no-visible-crosswalk.text: There is no visible pedestrian crossing here

ramp-required-unsure.text: Not sure if a drop kerb is required
ramp-required-unsure.tooltip-curb-ramp: Some alleyways or commercial driveways require ramps due to height differences, others do not. Sometimes it's not clear if a seam between a footpath requires a ramp or tactile surface indicator.

space-to-avoid-unsure.tooltip: The width of the footpath may be difficult to judge from a picture

too-minor-unsure.tooltip: It may be unclear whether an issue like grass between footpath blocks needs to be labeled

sidewalk-needed-unsure.text: Not sure if there should be a footpath here
sidewalk-needed-unsure.tooltip: Sometimes more context is necessary, and it's hard to determine if a footpath is necessary from just one image
